key_insight: The QICK Box is a modular, open-source RF front-end for quantum control and readout that combines flexible hardware with low-latency software/firmware to serve multiple quantum platforms.
engineering_relevance: It provides a scalable control/readout architecture with up to 16 outputs, 8 inputs, and 8 DC biases, making it useful for superconducting, atomic, ion-trapped, spin-defect, sensor, and networked quantum systems.
method: Modular output and input daughtercards support either fast DC-coupled or RF signal chains up to 10 GHz.
Software-controlled power levels, step attenuation, and bandpass filtering tune the signal path for different experiments.
System performance was validated on a six-transmon testbed with single-shot readout measurements.
evidence_signal: On a six-transmon device at QUIET, the system achieved 91.7 +/- 0.4% readout fidelity and 4.4 +/- 0.1 SNR without a quantum amplifier.
watch_item: Readout fidelity is currently limited by T1 decay during measurement, so device coherence and measurement timing remain critical.
paper_title: The QICK Box: A Modular RF Front-End System for Quantum Control and Readout
